title: Burst Capacity Playbook - SilverOak POC Kickoff
summary: Kickoff to scope a 4-week POC focused on burst capacity and token-tail behavior. Goal: define success criteria (99th latency, cost/GPU efficiency), collect sample traffic and tokenized payloads, run Redwood-hosted benchmark and a dedicated-run comparison. Discussed concurrency patterns, burst duration distribution, cold start concerns, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: customer to share sample payloads and SLA targets; Redwood to share benchmark template and run an initial baseline next week.
topics: Workload shape (baseline QPS, burst peaks, burst duration)
Concurrency mapping to slots and expected tail latency
Benchmark design: synthetic replay vs live ramp
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, fallback model strategies
Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, it is 15:00 UTC, we have about an hour, we're gonna run through the workload and line up success criteria. 
[00:12] Priya Nair: thanks Avery, appreciate you squeezing us in. quick context, we're building a risk-scoring microservice used in loan origination flows, typical request attaches user history + 3-4 prompts, um we're latency sensitive but also cost conscious.
[00:24] Diego Morales: cool, can you give us rough numbers? baseline qps, peak qps, how long bursts last?
[00:30] Marcus Lee: baseline is around 60 qps, peaks go to ~720 qps during morning batch lane for 30-45s, we also see longer tails where sustained 200-300 qps for 10-12 minutes during market opens.
[00:42] Avery Chen: good, so short high spikes and longer medium-length elevated periods. what's the typical prompt size? input tokens? output?
[00:48] Priya Nair: input avg ~110 tokens, p95 about 340 when history grows, output average 160 tokens, p95 ~420. these are after our own truncation heuristics, also ~12% of calls include an external doc embed (embedding returned separately), sometimes we fold that in at different stages.
[01:05] Diego Morales: great detail. for the POC we'll need token histograms, even a small CSV with per-request input_len/output_len and timestamp is perfect — that lets us synthesize a realistic replay.
[01:16] Sofia Gutierrez: on security, we need to confirm that Redwood can integrate with our KMS for key management, and audit logs retained for 12 months, plus SSO through Okta. Also any egress controls for private deployment?
[01:27] Leah Patel: yes we support customer-managed KMS for Private, Hosted can use envelope encryption with customer keys if required, audit logs are available in the console and downloadable for compliance. We'll follow up with SOC2 artifacts.
[01:39] Ethan Brooks: latency SLO: our bar is 95th < 250ms for short prompts and 99th < 600ms — is that realistic?
[01:46] Diego Morales: depends on model and deployment mode — hosted with an XL-ish open model might hit that for shorter prompts; for long outputs 99th under 600ms is ambitious but we can target it and measure. We'll likely need batching knobs and caching.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: curious about cold starts — we have endpoints that scale down to zero at night. We can't afford 2-3s cold starts.
[02:04] Avery Chen: understood. we do have warm pool strategies in Dedicated and keepalive heuristics in Hosted; for strict cold-start SLAs we'd recommend a dedicated minimum instance pool or a short keepalive. We'll include warmup run patterns in the benchmark.
[02:16] Priya Nair: how do you model burst tails? our ops want 99.9th percentile over a 24hr window to be stable not just synthetic ramp tests.
[02:24] Diego Morales: good, we'll do two benchmark modes: (1) replay of real traffic using your CSV with timestamped arrival — this captures burstiness and temporal clustering; (2) stress bursts for short durations (10-60s) with exponential arrivals to push concurrency. For tail capture we recommend multiple runs across windows and compute rolling-quantiles.
[02:40] Marcus Lee: any automatic fallback to a smaller model to keep latency/cost predictable?
[02:44] Avery Chen: yes, Redwood routing supports policy-based fallback — route to quantized variant or smaller model when latency exceeds threshold or when capacity constrained. We'll show cost/latency tradeoffs in the POC.
[02:55] Sofia Gutierrez: also need to log inputs for debugging but we have PHI in some fields, so we need redact-by-field and retention controls.
[03:02] Leah Patel: we can configure field-level redaction, and Redwood can disable retention for specific routes. We'll add that to the security checklist.
[03:10] Ethan Brooks: what's the expected timeline for the POC milestones?
[03:13] Avery Chen: proposed 4 weeks: week 0 (this week) gather traffic and success criteria; week 1 run baseline hosted benchmarks; week 2 run dedicated sizing and tuned configs; week 3 run follow-ups and finalize recommendations + cost model. We can compress if you want an accelerated 2-week run but it adds some risk.
[03:28] Priya Nair: 4 weeks sounds OK. can you run a hosted baseline first then dedicated comparisons — we'll need both numbers to justify procurement.
[03:36] Diego Morales: yes. for sizing we'll map your peak concurrency to slots; rough rule of thumb: concurrency = QPS * avg_response_time_seconds. Using your numbers 720 qps * ~0.5s equals 360 concurrency peak — we'll validate with token-size-aware perf numbers.
[03:51] Marcus Lee: that math makes sense but we saw higher apparent concurrency due to open KV cache lookups — does that change anything?
[03:58] Diego Morales: it can; KV cache miss patterns increase per-request compute and can inflate tail; we'll instrument cache hit/miss in the replay and run a cache-warmed vs cache-cold comparison.
[04:08] Priya Nair: about telemetry — what do you need from us for the replay?
[04:11] Leah Patel: ideally CSV rows: timestamp_iso, input_tokens, output_tokens, route_id, user_bucket(optional), cache_hit_flag(optional). If you can't export that, a sampled JSON dump with these fields works. Also a few representative payloads for tokenization edge-cases (long history, long doc).
[04:27] Priya Nair: we can deliver that by Friday EOD.
[04:30] Marcus Lee: and what about cost modeling — can you show cost per 10k tokens and per-concurrency slot?
[04:35] Avery Chen: yes we'll produce a cost model comparing hosted vs reserved Dedicated instances, factoring in batching and prefix caching benefits. We'll show cost sensitivity to average output length and burst frequency.
[04:47] Sofia Gutierrez: do you do per-route RBAC? we need to lock down who can call high-priv routes.
[04:51] Leah Patel: yes RBAC roles can be per-route and integrated with your IdP. We'll add role examples to the security pack.
[04:57] Ethan Brooks: on benchmarks, what metrics do you capture?
[05:00] Diego Morales: p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, tokens/sec, cost per token, concurrency profile over time, error rates, model version diff. We'll also produce a tail-latency heatmap and burst frequency histogram.
[05:14] Priya Nair: can you simulate external embedding calls? sometimes we call an external vector store and that introduces jitter.
[05:20] Diego Morales: yes we can inject artificial downstream latencies into the replay or model them as upstream dependency delays. We'll flag those in the results so you can separate model inference from system jitter.
[05:30] Marcus Lee: competitor question — we're also talking to Anthropic on managed infra and evaluating Vertex AI. How does Redwood differentiate here?
[05:36] Avery Chen: short answer: production-first observability and cost controls — we give token-level cost breakdowns, prefix caching, and routing policies plus a unified private and hosted experience. We'll surface benchmarking reproducibility too.
[05:48] Priya Nair: sounds good. ok let's recap next steps.
[05:51] Avery Chen: recap: 1) SilverOak to share CSV of timestamped tokens + 10 representative payloads by Friday. 2) Redwood to share benchmark template and security pack (SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration notes) by Tuesday. 3) Redwood to run hosted baseline with your data next Wednesday and share preliminary dashboard. 4) schedule dedicated sizing run the following week. Anyone object?
[06:11] Marcus Lee: no objections.
[06:12] Sofia Gutierrez: fine.
[06:13] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[06:15] Avery Chen: great thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and calendar invites.
[06:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels, some filler words removed for readability, timestamps are approximate. There was brief crosstalk when discussing burst math.
